refs.title: Cottage Lawn - Wikipedia
refs.note: Its whole description, which is the only fabric account this record carries: 'It is a two-story L-shaped house, with basement and attic. It is constructed of brick and coated in stucco. It features six quatrefoil columns that support Tudor arches spanning the verandah.'

refs.title: William J. Rotch Gothic Cottage -- National Historic Landmark Nomination
refs.note: Not about this house, and cited because it places it: the nomination names 'Cottage Lawn in Oneida, New York' as one of three other Davis Gothic Revival cottages listed on the National Register.

note: Tranche 2, Gothic Revival and picturesque villa cluster, 5 Sep 2026. NO HABS SURVEY: a loc.gov pictures search for 'Cottage Lawn Oneida New York' failed to fetch twice and no HABS item for the house surfaced in any other query; recorded as unresolved rather than as absent. Note that the quatrefoil column is the detail the Kingscote survey independently records on its own east porch -- two Gothic villas by two different architects, ten years and 250 miles apart, using the same section. No rights line is recorded: no Library item page was opened for this building.
